source.title: Function Induction and Task Generalization: An Interpretability Study with Off-by-One Addition
source.authors: Qinyuan Ye; Robin Jia; Xiang Ren

page_placements.theme: Abstract induction in pretrained LLMs (semantic, concept, function, category, entity, symbolic, latent)

record.tranche_reason: Extends the induction-head idea to a higher-level function-induction circuit in pretrained language models and reports results on that related construct; it does not measure conventional token-copying induction heads or their formation during training.
record.gate_note: The paper distinguishes its function-induction mechanism (inducing an arithmetic or other function) from token-level induction heads ([A][B] … [A] → [B]). Its own results concern function induction and task performance, not the conventional token-copying behaviour in the claim versions. It does not track training over time, loss bumps, or in-context-learning loss by token index. Rows below record results about the related function-induction mechanism; none directly test a listed claim version. Some plotted results have no numerical values in the text.
record.test_reason: The study analyses 'function induction' (previous-token heads plus FI heads inducing f(x)=x+1) in pretrained 7–9B LMs. It never measures conventional token-copying induction heads, their formation, their phase change, or loss by token index. The structural analogy to induction heads is the authors' framing, not a test of any version. None of its results bear on V1–V7 as stated, so it is T6 rather than T3. The FI-vs-FV comparison and the reuse findings concern a different construct and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also stress that the +1 function is split across several FI heads in parallel, each writing a distinct piece. They say the mechanism extends, rather than tests, prior induction-head and function-vector findings, and they leave its emergence during pretraining to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses path patching, head ablations, and causal effects on arithmetic and related task pairs in pretrained models; it does not reproduce the original training-time measurement or token-copying induction-head method.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with model, task, number range, offset, and which heads are ablated. Six FI heads leave non-zero performance on shifted MMLU and ROT-2; nine heads reduce those results further. Toy-model outcomes differ by training-data mixture.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma-2 9B, off-by-one addition runs through previous-token heads feeding function-induction heads, plus consolidation heads. Ablating 6 FI heads drops contrast accuracy from 86% to 0%, while ablating random heads has minimal effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An induction-like circuit operating on functions rather than tokens mediates in-context induction of a +1 function in pretrained LMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Analogous three-group circuits are found in Llama-3 8B, Mistral-v0.1 7B and Llama-2 7B. In Llama-2 the induced function leans toward x+2. Llama-2's FI heads in layers 29–31 do not overlap with Todd et al.'s function-vector heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Function-induction heads recur across pretrained model families and are distinct from function-vector heads.

fits_no_version.finding: The same FI heads are reused for off-by-k addition, shifted MMLU, Caesar cipher and base-8 addition. They are incomplete for MMLU (12% remains after 6-head ablation) and ROT-2 (36% remains), and three extra heads take both to about 0%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single function-induction circuit is reused across counterfactual two-step in-context tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: For Mistral-v0.1 and Gemma-2, off-by-one accuracy is higher when the test answer appears among the in-context answers (Fig. 12). The authors suggest these models lean on copy-paste induction more than function induction, but say more rigorous analysis is needed. This is figure-only and no row records it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Token-copying induction contributes to few-shot arithmetic performance in some pretrained LMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Small 3-layer transformers trained on mixtures of off-by-k addition tasks fail to infer the task in context; on k=1 they appear to average k=0 and k=2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context inference of the offset in toy addition models depends on training data and curriculum.

record.problems: The authors state that their identified circuit does not perfectly satisfy faithfulness and completeness; the reported faithfulness score is 78.4% before local-search additions. The work focuses on a narrow set of synthetic or algorithmic tasks and pretrained models. Many plotted accuracy and causal-effect values are not given numerically in the text. The toy-model results are preliminary and averaged over 5 runs.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant results were left out under the 60-row limit. Results about generic task accuracies and other analyses were omitted where they did not report an outcome on the function-induction mechanism or its task behaviour.

untested.parts: No small attention-only models. Conventional token-copying induction and its composition with a previous-token head are not measured; only the function-level analogue in pretrained LMs.
No training dynamics, abruptness, loss bump or coincident in-context-learning gain.
No loss-by-token-index measure. No test of whether token induction heads carry most in-context learning.
Token-copying induction heads are not identified across models. FI heads across four families concern a different construct.
Toy-model data mixtures change task accuracy, but induction-head formation and timing are not measured.
Conventional induction heads are not compared against other heads for few-shot task learning. The FI/FV disjointness concerns non-token-copying heads only.
No formation sub-steps or transitions are measured.

record.verdict_notes: Neither the record's reader nor this check finds any row bearing on V1–V7. The Fig. 12 copy-vs-function observation is the closest to V6 or V3, but it involves no head-level measurement of token induction heads. The authors' related work cites Yin & Steinhardt (FV heads may evolve from induction heads) and Minegishi et al. (multi-phase circuit emergence); these are cited results, not this study's. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The paper studies a function-level circuit in pretrained models, not small attention-only transformers implementing token copying through previous-token and induction heads.
No training-time emergence, abruptness, loss bump, or coincident gain in in-context learning is measured.
The paper does not measure loss falling with token index in large transformers or whether conventional induction heads cause most such in-context learning.
It reports function-induction circuits across several pretrained model families, but does not measure conventional induction behaviour across training runs, other architectures, or modalities.
Toy-model training-data mixtures are varied, but formation of conventional induction heads and their timing are not measured.
The paper tests function-induction heads on counterfactual and related tasks, not whether conventional induction heads are or are not the main carrier of ordinary few-shot task learning.
No training-time sequence of formation sub-steps or overlapping transitions is measured.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 (9B)
rows.operation_detail: Path patching to output logits identified heads with relative logit difference |r| > 2%; the paper grouped them as consolidation, function-induction (FI), and previous-token (PT) heads.
rows.measure: Identified head groups and their roles in the function-induction circuit
rows.value: 10 attention heads directly influenced output logits; subsequent patching identified Group 3 heads writing to Group 2 head values. At answer positions, Group 3 heads attended to the preceding '=' token.
rows.note: The paper interprets this as function-level induction, not conventional token-copying induction heads.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 (9B), H39.7
rows.operation_detail: Path-patched the head's value and measured relative logit difference when patching to final output.
rows.note: H39.7 is described as a representative FI head; this is evidence about the paper's function-induction task.

source_check.correct: H39.7 has r = −27% when patching to the final output. Setting H39.7's value as the target node is a separate experiment identifying upstream previous-token heads.

relation.reason: The authors explain and compare the conventional induction-head mechanism with their function-induction circuit, without directly testing the catalog's claim versions.

tranche.reason: The study measures function induction in arithmetic and related tasks, a different construct from the catalog's token-copying induction-head claims. It does not test their training-time formation, phase change, or contribution to token-index loss.

source_check.notes: The cross-model findings concern function induction. Llama-2 is a weaker case: §E.1 reports 6% off-by-one accuracy and an aggregate induced function leaning toward x + 2.
